latin: Non punitur Rex terrae in terra, quin prius humilietur militia coelestis in coelo.
latin_note: The 1487 reprint misread 'punitur' as 'ponitur', an error Farmer states 'was followed by all later Renaissance editors of Pico's text' (paraphrase of Farmer's note; the apparatus variant itself is recorded at farmer1998:18416).
translation: The king of the earth is not punished on earth, unless the heavenly host is first humbled in heaven.
translation_note: Follows the 1486 reading 'punitur' ('is punished') rather than the 1487 misprint 'ponitur' ('is placed'), per Farmer's note (farmer1998:18463).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch12, from Latin at farmer1998:18406
doctrine: Farmer's note states that both texts Wirszubski (1989: 51) proposes as potential sources emphasize 'the favorite Pichean theme that proportion exists between higher and lower realms', here expressed in an eschatological register (paraphrase, farmer1998:18463). He also records the transmission error by which the 1487 reprint read 'ponitur' for 'punitur', an error followed, in his words, 'by all later Renaissance editors of Pico's text' (paraphrase, farmer1998:18463).
historiography: Wirszubski quotes the thesis as his 'Conclusio XLVI' and states that 'what this thesis states is not, strictly speaking, a specifically Kabbalistic' claim, though the excerpt consulted breaks off before he completes the point (wirszubski1989:2939).
